correctness.rationale: F25=F5[omega]/(omega^2-2) and square differences give a 25-vertex 12-regular Paley graph; independently reconstructed all cliques with face vector (25,150,250,75,15), Euler characteristic65. The package finite verifier validates 15 free (3,4)-simplex collapse pairs and 60 free (2,3)-pairs, leaving a connected 2-complex. Independently reconstructed the 1-skeleton spanning-tree group presentation: 24 tree edges,126 non-tree generators,250 triangular relators; repeated exact lawful cyclic Tietze eliminations remove all 126 generators and leave no nontrivial relators, establishing pi1=1 (not merely H1=0). A simply connected finite 2-complex with chi65 has free H2=Z^64 and no other positive-dimensional homology, hence by Hurewicz/Whitehead is homotopy equivalent to wedge_{64} S2. Independently enumerated all 600 semiaffine transformations x->ux^{5^e}+b with square u; each acts simplicially and signed Lefschetz fixed-simplex traces give distribution {-16:15,-1:72,0:450,4:62,64:1}. Because H0=Q and sole positive rational homology H2, the reduced Lefschetz sum equals actual H2 trace, not just virtual character. Character average is 0, hence no G-invariant H2. Existing general Latin-square graph homology and translation-character conclusions are credited as prior, not new.
residual_risks: Finite exact presentation and elementary collapses establish this single graph; no theorem for all Paley orders, and the trace calculation concerns exactly the specified 600-map semiaffine group. Independently reran the 126 Tietze eliminations; legal high-dimensional collapses were assessed by reading complete verifier and its free-face tests, not independently reproduced in separate script.

evidence: Theorem3.12 supplies homology of all Latin-square graph clique complexes over every field: H2=(n-1)^3-I(M), H1=0, higher homology=0, with Proposition3.13 on boundary Smith factors. At n=5 no intercalates, H2=64. These prior results do not assert simple connectivity or the full semiaffine character.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General homology theorems cover the numeric Betti and torsion portions and must not be treated as novelty. A general cohomology vanishing theorem alone does not logically imply pi1 trivial (perfect fundamental groups exist), and no inspected general G-character theorem includes this 600-element action.
